title: TAG Video Systems and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Partner to Bring Broadcast Monitoring to OCI
body_html:
What Was Announced

TAG Video Systems and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure have partnered to bring broadcast monitoring to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), a move that aims to simplify the deployment and integration of monitoring systems for broadcast workflows. This partnership allows TAG's monitoring solutions to be hosted on OCI, providing a cloud-based platform for media companies to monitor their broadcast feeds. By leveraging OCI's cloud infrastructure, TAG's solutions can be easily scaled and integrated with existing broadcast systems, reducing the complexity and cost associated with traditional on-premise monitoring systems.

The Engineering and Operational Significance

The partnership between TAG Video Systems and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is significant because it addresses a key challenge in broadcast monitoring: the need for scalable and flexible monitoring systems that can handle the complexities of modern broadcast workflows. By hosting TAG's monitoring solutions on OCI, media companies can take advantage of the cloud's scalability and flexibility to monitor their broadcast feeds in real-time, without the need for expensive and complex on-premise infrastructure. This partnership also enables the integration of TAG's monitoring solutions with other cloud-based broadcast systems, such as playout, ingest, and media asset management (MAM) systems, allowing for a more streamlined and automated broadcast workflow. Furthermore, the use of OCI's cloud infrastructure provides a high level of redundancy and failover, ensuring that monitoring systems remain operational even in the event of an outage or disaster.

Industry Context

The partnership between TAG Video Systems and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure reflects a broader trend in the broadcast industry towards cloud-based workflows and software-defined systems. As media companies increasingly adopt IP-based infrastructures, such as SMPTE ST 2110, and move towards more flexible and scalable broadcast systems, the need for cloud-based monitoring solutions has grown. Other companies, such as Telestream and AWS, have also partnered to provide cloud-based monitoring solutions, highlighting the demand for flexible and scalable monitoring systems in the broadcast industry. The use of cloud-based monitoring systems also enables the adoption of new technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML), to enhance the monitoring and analysis of broadcast feeds. Additionally, the partnership between TAG and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure demonstrates the importance of interoperability and collaboration between vendors in the broadcast industry, as media companies seek to create more integrated and automated workflows.

Implications for Broadcast and Media Teams

The partnership between TAG Video Systems and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure has significant implications for broadcast and media teams, as it provides a more flexible and scalable solution for monitoring broadcast feeds. Engineers and operations managers should take note of the potential for cloud-based monitoring systems to simplify their workflows and reduce the complexity and cost associated with traditional on-premise monitoring systems. Additionally, the integration of TAG's monitoring solutions with other cloud-based broadcast systems enables the creation of more automated and streamlined workflows, allowing media companies to focus on content creation and delivery rather than infrastructure management. As the broadcast industry continues to evolve towards more software-defined and cloud-based systems, media companies will need to evaluate their monitoring systems and consider the benefits of cloud-based solutions, such as scalability, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness, to remain competitive and efficient in the market. Furthermore, the use of cloud-based monitoring systems also enables media companies to take advantage of new technologies, such as AI and ML, to enhance their monitoring and analysis capabilities, and to improve the overall quality and reliability of their broadcast feeds.
